takeaway: Warthin tumour (papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum): benign, almost only parotid, male smokers aged 40-60, cystic spaces with double epithelial layer, 10% bilateral and 10% multifocal.

question.text: A 65-year-old lifelong smoker has a 3 cm parotid lump; histology shows an encapsulated mass with cystic spaces lined by a double layer of epithelium. Most likely diagnosis?

lines.text: Think of the smoker with a lump in the parotid gland. People who smoke are eight times more likely to develop it.
It is also called papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum, hence the little lymph node hat on our warthog.
Under the microscope, you see an encapsulated mass with narrow cystic spaces lined by a double layer of cells.
It is benign, arises almost only in the parotid, and is more common in men aged forty to sixty.
So, smoker, parotid lump, double layer: Warthin tumour.
